text: Inhibitory histone methyltransferases (HMTs) act as gene-specific gatekeepers, preventing unliganded nuclear receptors from binding target promoters and requiring demethylases such as LSD1 for ligand/signal-dependent activation, thereby circumventing pathological constitutive gene induction. In bovine somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT), eight-cell embryos display global hypermethylation of H3K9me3/2; the H3K9 demethylases KDM4D and KDM4E mediate active demethylation in IVF embryos but are deficient in cloned embryos at embryonic genome activation (EGA). KDM4E is the more crucial factor: its overexpression restores the transcriptome, improves blastocyst formation and cloning efficiency, and RNA–KDM4E interactions are essential for H3K9 demethylation during EGA. Finally, base-pair-resolution mouse methylomes in stem cells and neuronal progenitors reveal low-methylated regions (LMRs) averaging 30% methylation—CpG-poor distal regulatory regions shaped by DNA-binding factors.
